questions.stemHtml: What is the action of marked muscle in the given image?
questions.solutionHtml:
Elevation

Marked muscle in the image is temporalis. Temporalis elevates the mandible and so closes the mouth and approximates the teeth.

The muscle also contributes to side-to-side grinding movements. The posterior fibers retract the mandible after it has been protruded. The posterior fibers of temporalis, which are almost horizontal, are the only source of mandibular retrusion.

Temporalis muscle




BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 3, Page No-125.

questions.stem: Which of the following bones is not involved in wrist joint formation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ulna

Radiocarpal (wrist) joint

  • It is a synovial ellipsoid joint.
  • It is formed by articulation of the distal end of the radius and the articular disc above and the scaphoid, lunate, and triquetral bones below.
  • Ulna is excluded from the wrist joint by the articular disc.
  • Radius’s distal end articulates with the scaphoid and lunate bones of the hand at the wrist joint and with the ulna at the distal radioulnar joint.


BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 3, Page No-171.

questions.stemHtml: Occlusion of the artery supplying marked areas will cause all except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Apraxia
  • Marked area is the paracentral lobule, bounded posteriorly by the marginal ramus and anteriorly by the paracentral sulcus (a branch of the cingulate sulcus), and contains the distal part of the central sulcus.
  • Function: Motor and sensory innervations of the contralateral lower extremity regulation of physiological function such as defecation and micturition.
  • Injury to the area can cause contralateral lower limb muscle weakness, urinary and fecal incontinence, and perianal anesthesia.


BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 3, Page No-142.

questions.stem: All the given muscles help in inversion of foot except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Peroneus longus

Peroneus longus and brevis are major evertors of the foot whereas running to the medial side of ankle (of both anterior and posterior compartment) like tibialis anterior, flexor digitorum longus, and long tendons of great toe act as invertors of foot.

  • Inversion: Medial border of the foot is raised so that the sole faces inside.
  • Eversion: Lateral border of the foot is raised so that the sole faces outside.
  • Inversion and eversion occur mainly at intertarsal joints.
  • Major movements occur at the Talo-calcaneo-navicular joint.
  • Other involved joints are transverse tarsal/midtarsal joints.


BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 2, Page No-112,117.

questions.stem: Left superior intercostal vein drains into:
questions.solutionHtml:
Brachiocephalic vein
  • The left superior intercostal vein is formed by the second, third, and fourth posterior intercostal veins and drains into the left brachiocephalic vein.

Left superior intercostal vein




BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 1, Page No-247.

questions.stem: Ligamentum flavum consists of:
questions.solutionHtml:
Elastin

Ligamentum flavum connects the laminae of adjacent vertebral canal.

  • Ligaments, tendons, capsule usually are composed of Type 1 collagen fibers which are also present in ligamentum flavum but its predominant tissue is yellow elastin tissue which prevents buckling of the ligament into the spinal canal during extension.
  • The ligamentum flavum has a high content of elastin. So under tension it can be stretched by 80% without damage.
  • Functions of ligamentum flavum are to provide a constant smooth lining to the vertebral canal, which is never overstretched in flexion and which never goes back in extension.


Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-831, 867.e1.

questions.stem: A Patient with syphilis develops an imbalance in walking with eyes closed and has to lift up foot and stamp on the ground to walk. Name the tract involved in the given condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Dorsal column tract
  • Destruction of dorsal column tract due to tertiary syphilis. Often fasciculus gracilis is involved bilaterally. Patient has a wide-based, staggering gait accompanied by slapping foot against the ground while walking.
  • Positive Romberg’s sign is also mentioned in the question as the patient is unable to walk with closed eyes because of loss of conscious proprioception.

The clinical scenarios are:

  • Patient with syphilis
  • Imbalance on walking with eyes closed: Suggests sensory ataxia and positive Romberg’s sign
  • Stamping gait: Due to defective proprioception (a feature of dorsal column affection)


BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 4, Page No-50,51.

questions.stem: Golgi apparatus in serous acinar cells is at:
questions.solutionHtml:
Supranuclear

Serous cells

Serous cells have a pyramidal shape, with a relatively wide basal surface facing the basal lamina and a small apical surface facing the lumen of the acinus. They contain large amounts of rER, free ribosomes, a prominent Golgi apparatus, and numerous spherical secretory granules.

As in most protein-secreting cells that store their secretions in zymogen granules, the granules are located in the apical cytoplasm.

Golgi complex (GC) is seen mainly close to the nucleus in supranuclear position (figure).




Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-659,660.

questions.stem: Which of the following fibers reach Purkinje cells directly?
questions.solutionHtml:
Inferior olivary nucleus
  • Only fibers reaching Purkinje cells directly in the outer molecular layer are climbing fibers originating from inferior olivary nucleus of medulla oblongata constituting olivocerebellar and para olivocerebellar tract.
  • Rest all other tracts are called Mossy fibers.


Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-469-473.

questions.stem: What is normally seen in the lumbar spine?
questions.solutionHtml:
Lordosis

Vertebral Column curvatures

  • Normal lordosis is the two forward curves seen in the neck (cervical spine) and low back (lumbar spine).
  • Normal kyphosis is the two backward curves seen in the chest (thoracic spine and hip areas (sacral spine).
  • Each of the naturally occurring and normal soft curves serves to distribute mechanical stress incurred as the body is at rest and during movement.



Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-819-821.

questions.stemHtml: Which of the marked areas is involved in relieving pain when a painful site is massaged?
questions.solutionHtml:
A

Gate-Control Theory

  • The first and best known of these theories is gate control theory, in which the cold causes stimulation of Aβ afferent nerve fibers, which in turn inhibit transmission of pain to second-order neurons through gating at the substantia gelatinosa in the dorsal root ganglion of the spinal cord.
  • The Marked Area A is substantia gelatinosa.


Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-428.

questions.stemHtml: What is the type of connective tissue marked as an arrow in the below image?
questions.solutionHtml:
Dense irregular

Dermis layer of Skin

Reticular layer

Papillary layer

Most superficial layer of dermis; composed of areolar connective tissue; forms dermal papillae; contains subpapillary vascular plexus.

Reticular layer

Deeper layer of dermis; dense irregular connective tissue surrounding hair follicles, sebaceous glands and sweat glands, nerves, and deep plexus of blood vessels extending into subcutaneous layer.

  • The marked area is reticular dermis.
  • It is composed of dense irregular collagenous connective tissue (most commonly type I collagen) containing the usual array of connective tissue elements, including cells, blood, and lymphatic vessels.
  • Sweat gland and cutaneous nerves are also present and their branches extend into the papillary layer and into the epidermis.



I B Singh Histology:8th edition page No-48,50.

questions.stem: Which is the correct pairing of lymph nodes and their anatomical boundaries?
questions.solutionHtml:
Level 6–hyoid to clavicle

Vertical chain of Lymph node

Vertical chain

Level 1 consists of submental, submandibular nodes

Level 2 consists of upper jugular nodes

Level 3 consists of middle jugular group

Level 4 consists of lower jugular group

Level 5 consists of posterior triangle group

Level 6 consists of anterior compartment group

Level 7 consists of superior mediastinal group

Level 8 consists of supraclavicular nodes

Level 9 consists of retropharyngeal nodes




Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-594,595.

questions.stemHtml: Identify the nerve (marked by white arrow) in the given section of cranial cavity:
questions.solutionHtml:
Oculomotor

Nerves emerging out from Cranial foramina

Structure passing through the cranial cavity

  • Oculomotor nerve emerges at the midbrain on the medial side of the crus of the cerebral peduncle and passes between the superior cerebellar and posterior cerebral arteries and runs forward in the interpeduncular cistern on the lateral side of the posterior communicating artery to reach cavernous sinus.
  • It enters the cavernous sinus by piercing the posterior part of the roof on the lateral side of the posterior clinoid process and descends along the lateral dural wall of the cavernous sinus, dividing into superior and inferior divisions which run beneath the trochlear and ophthalmic nerve.



Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-565-567.

questions.stem: Which of the following cranial nerves is not associated with olfaction?
questions.solutionHtml:
XII
  • XII nerve is a motor nerve and has no role in gestation and olfaction.
  • Lingual branch of V transmits taste to chorda tympani, X carries taste from posterior 1/3rd of the tongue and vagus and also supplies taste buds of pharynx and epiglottic Part.
  • Taste and olfaction go hand in hand. So based on the options given, the answer will be XII nerve.


Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-643-645.
